# Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice

## Original exercise

James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
\(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).

> 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
> prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.

## Definitions and complete target

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183:

source_steps.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Use N001 and H002 to count |I|=n. By H005 choose an integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V; its cardinality is n since the e basis of N001 has n elements. Tensoring the integer coordinate isomorphism with R gives R-coordinates on M_R: finite sums ∑_{i∈I}r_i⊗m_i have unique coefficients r_i∈R. Explicitly the coordinate homomorphisms of M extend to these coordinates, and the sum map is their inverse. Under iota these basis tensors go to m_i, still complex-linearly independent, so iota is injective. This proves freeness of rank n and shows its image spans V over ℂ. Admissibility H005 gives preservation of M by every X_r,Y_r; extension by R gives preservation of M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve them; h=xy−yx by H003 preserves them too.

Fix i,j∈I. Evaluate using N001. X_λ kills e_k for k<λ and takes e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Therefore Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ. Also X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, so X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ. In Pi Y_(λ−j), an input e_k with kj goes past the end and is zero. At k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,j); hence Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Since λ

Compose the identities F002. On the e basis, E_iλ E_λj=E_ij; thus E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002. Consequently E_ij preserves M_R for all i,j. Together with F001 and F002 these are the asserted lattice and matrix-unit identities. This reasoning has used distinct complex weights only in N001 and makes no assertion about distinct weights modulo p.

By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. For any c∈J_j, the preserving map E_ij of N002 sends c e_j to c e_i, so c∈J_i. Interchanging i and j gives J_i=J_j. Thus all these R-submodules equal J=J_0.

For arbitrary u∈M_R, choose its coordinates d using the e basis N001: iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k. Applying E_ii and N002 gives d_i e_i∈iota(M_R), so d_i∈J_i=J by F001. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. Consequently the sum-of-coordinates map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear bijection, with inverse the coordinate projections, and M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k after the injective identification iota of N002.

By N002, M_R has n generators over R. The image of these generators under E_ii generates J e_i by F001. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise F002 would give M_R=0, whose complex span is zero, contrary to N002 and the nonempty basis of V in N001. Thus F001 and F002 give the full common-module and direct-sum assertions.

Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the images 1⊗c0 of a finite generating set of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. The multiplication map is given on pure tensors by ρ⊗c0↦ρc0∈ℂ, with ρ∈ℚ and c0∈J; it is well-defined by R-balancing. Since ℚ is the fraction field of R⊂ℚ (H001), a common nonzero denominator in R combines any finite tensor sum into d0^(-1)⊗c0 with 0≠d0∈R and c0∈J. The image of such an expression is c0/d0; a zero image implies c0=0 and hence a zero tensor. Thus multiplication is injective and identifies QJ with the rational span of J.

Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. N002 states that M_R is free of rank n, so M002 gives dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R M_R)=n. Tensoring the coordinate isomorphism of N003 gives ℚ⊗_R M_R≅∏_{i∈I}QJ: on a pure tensor with coordinates (gamma_i), the map sends ρ⊗(∑_{i∈I}gamma_i e_i) to (ρ⊗gamma_i)_{i∈I}; inverse maps insert the coordinates and sum. These inverse maps are balanced and linear, so this identification needs no flatness assumption. Apply M001 with A=ℚ, B=I and constant family C_i=QJ. Here I is finite with |I|=n by N001; QJ is a finite-dimensional vector space by F001, hence free and finitely generated. We obtain dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}QJ)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. Therefore n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, r=1.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonempty tuple g_1,…,g_k of nonzero generators of J, as permitted by N003. By F001 and F002, J lies in a one-dimensional rational line, and its nonzero vector a spans that line. Consequently each g_j=q_j a with a nonzero rational q_j. This proves the rational-coordinate description of a generating set; it is derived from the rank calculation rather than assumed merely from J⊂ℂ.

For each nonzero rational q_j, strip the factors p from its integer numerator and denominator. Since p is prime by H001, this gives q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j, with eta_j=ν_j∈ℤ and both numerator and denominator of u_j prime to p. Thus u_j and u_j^(-1) are in R. Put ν=min_j eta_j, which exists for the nonempty finite tuple of F003, and b=p^ν a≠0. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j−ν)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j−ν≥0. Conversely, for any generator attaining the minimum, multiplication of that generator by its unit u_j^(-1) gives b; hence b∈J and Rb⊆J. The first inclusion on generators gives J⊆Rb, so J=Rb.

N003 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}Rb e_i. Its coordinate sum map shows that (b e_i) spans over R; since b≠0 and the e family is complex-linearly independent by N001, it is R-linearly independent. Thus it is an R-basis. The same reasoning works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001 and F002 this proves the asserted rank and basis conclusions, exporting existence of such b without fixing its private identity.

The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. 1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and independent endpoint-fidelity Audit B remain required.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero

45: abbrev Function.Surjective.moduleLeft {R S M : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
46:     [Semiring S] [SMul S M] (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
47:     (hsmul : ∀ (c) (x : M), f c • x = c • x) : Module S M :=

49:     zero_smul := fun x => by rw [← f.map_zero, hsmul, zero_smul]
50:     add_smul := hf.forall₂.mpr fun a b x => by simp only [← f.map_add, hsmul, add_smul] }

59:     -- Porting note: the `show f (r + s) • x = f r • x + f s • x` wasn't needed in mathlib3.

61:     -- use in later fields.  See

63:     -- TODO(jmc): there should be a rw-lemma `smul_comp` close to `SMulZeroClass.compFun`
64:     add_smul := fun r s x => show f (r + s) • x = f r • x + f s • x by simp [add_smul] }

import Mathlib
noncomputable section
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LatticeSL2
def scalarRing (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(scalarRing p)
instance (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (scalarRing p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def divided {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev Ix (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
def Stable {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (a : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, a u ∈ W
def SimpleTriple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Stable W x → Stable W y → Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Preserves {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, a (m : V) ∈ M
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def LiftOf {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, (f m : V) = a (m : V)
def E {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Basis (Ix l) ℂ V) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
end LatticeSL2
types: LatticeSL2.R p
LatticeSL2.MR p M
LatticeSL2.VK K M
(algebraMap (LatticeSL2.R p) ℚ)
IsScalarTower (LatticeSL2.R p) ℂ V
∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M), Module.End K (LatticeSL2.VK K M)
@LinearMap.baseChange
@IsScalarTower.of_compHom

33:   algebraMap := ZMod.castHom h R
34:   smul := fun a r => cast a * r
35:   commutes' := fun a r =>
36:     show (cast a * r : R) = r * cast a by
37:       rcases ZMod.intCast_surjective a with ⟨k, rfl⟩
38:       change ZMod.castHom h R k * r = r * ZMod.castHom h R k
39:       rw [map_intCast, Int.cast_comm]

45: instance since it creates a diamond with `Algebra.id`.

import Mathlib
noncomputable section
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LatticeSL2
def scalarRing (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(scalarRing p)
instance (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (scalarRing p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def divided {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev Ix (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
def Stable {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (a : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, a u ∈ W
def SimpleTriple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Stable W x → Stable W y → Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Preserves {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, a (m : V) ∈ M
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def LiftOf {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, (f m : V) = a (m : V)
def E {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) ℂ V) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] :
    IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
def L {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def J {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (e : V) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (L p M).comap ((LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ).smulRight e |>.restrictScalars (R p))
def pPart {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (Set.range (fun u : MR p M => (p : ℤ) • u))
abbrev Red {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := ZMod p ⊗[ℤ] MR p M
end LatticeSL2
open LatticeSL2
types: ∀ [hc : CharP K p], letI a := ZMod.algebra K p; Nonempty (K ⊗[ZMod p] Red p M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M)
∀ κ : R p →+* K, letI a := κ.toAlgebra; Nonempty (K ⊗[R p] MR p M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M)

artifact.header:
import Mathlib
noncomputable section
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LatticeSL2
def scalarRing (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(scalarRing p)
instance (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (scalarRing p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def divided {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev Ix (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
def Stable {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (a : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, a u ∈ W
def SimpleTriple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Stable W x → Stable W y → Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Preserves {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, a (m : V) ∈ M
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def LiftOf {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, (f m : V) = a (m : V)
def E {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) ℂ V) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] :
    IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
def L {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def J {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (e : V) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (L p M).comap ((LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ).smulRight e |>.restrictScalars (R p))
def pPart {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (Set.range (fun u : MR p M => (p : ℤ) • u))
abbrev Red {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := ZMod p ⊗[ℤ] MR p M
abbrev RK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  K ⊗[R p] MR p M
abbrev FK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharP K p] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  K ⊗[ZMod p] Red p M
def throughR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (RK κ M) :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K
def throughF {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharP K p]
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (FK p K M) :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  (((f.baseChange (R p)).restrictScalars ℤ).baseChange (ZMod p)).baseChange K
def matrixUnit {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) F U) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End F U :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
def genFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End F U) (b : Ix l → U) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ix l, x (b i) = if hi : 0 < i.val then
      ((l - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • b ⟨i.val - 1, Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le i.val 1) i.isLt⟩
      else 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Ix l, y (b i) = if hi : i.val + 1 < l.toNat + 1 then
      ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • b ⟨i.val + 1, hi⟩ else 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Ix l, h (b i) = ((l - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def iotaSpec {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r : R p) (m : M), f (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = (algebraMap (R p) ℂ r) • (m : V)
def canonicalR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (C : RK κ M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M) : Prop :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  ∀ (c : K) (r : R p) (m : M),
    C (c ⊗ₜ[R p] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (κ r * c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m
def pureR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (c : K) (u : MR p M) : RK κ M :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  c ⊗ₜ[R p] u
def canonicalF {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharP K p]
    (κ : R p →+* K) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (D : FK p K M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M) : Prop :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∀ (c : K) (a : ZMod p) (r : R p) (m : M),
    D (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (a ⊗ₜ[ℤ] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m))) =
      ((ZMod.cast a : K) * κ r * c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m
def basisOrigin {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] {l : ℤ}
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V)
    (β : Module.Basis (Ix l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ J p M (ev y v 0) ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧
  ∃ ι : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V, iotaSpec p M ι ∧ Function.Injective ι ∧
  ∃ B : Module.Basis (Ix l) (R p) (MR p M),
    (∀ i, ι (B i) = b • ev y v i.val) ∧
  ∃ κ : R p →+* K, ∃ C : RK κ M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M,
    canonicalR κ M C ∧ ∀ i, β i = C (pureR κ 1 (B i))
end LatticeSL2
open LatticeSL2

Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
 (∃ fx fy fh : Module.End ℤ M, LiftOf M x fx ∧ LiftOf M y fy ∧ LiftOf M h fh) ∧

artifact.representation: λ is the integer l; nonnegative exponents are Nat and I is Fin (l.toNat+1), identified with 0≤i≤λ using H002. V is an arbitrary complex module; x,y,h are its linear action endomorphisms. H003 records the sl₂ Chevalley relations, highest weight and complex irreducibility. M is an arbitrary Submodule ℤ V, equivalently an additive subgroup, with the integer/complex basis and divided-power stability in H005. R is the rational subring generated by inverses of integers not divisible by p; T006 proves it is exactly the specified ℤ_(p). Scalar actions use its inclusion R→ℚ→ℂ. MR is the actual R⊗ℤ M; its image L is used only through the checked iota in T006/T008. J is the coefficient submodule defined by membership in L. VK=K⊗ℤ M uses the tensor commutor identification with the source M⊗ℤ K. Operators are the actual scalar extensions of compatible integral endomorphisms; existence is proved, and compatible lifts are unique. Red=ZMod p⊗ℤ MR is identified with MR/pMR by T018, and FK is its extension to K. RK and FK install only canonical scalar actions internally. matrixUnit B i j sends B j to B i and other basis vectors to zero; multiplication of endomorphisms is composition with the right factor acting first. No Audit A note is a premise, verified Lean theorem or instance assumption; the two M declarations are used directly from pinned Mathlib.

steps.explanation: Simultaneous induction on the nonnegative lowering exponent using the three complex commutators. Nat exponents represent precisely nonnegative integer exponents.

∀ (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) ℂ V), (∀ i, B i = ev y v i.val) →

  ∀ u ∈ L p M, matrixUnit B i j u ∈ L p M)
steps.explanation: Compose the factor identities and use R-module closure to prove preservation by every matrix unit; collect all N002 conclusions.

steps.explanation: Project finite generators of M_R to obtain finite generation of J. Nonzero complex span excludes J=0. Retain the common-module equalities and explicit coordinate isomorphism as N003.

steps.statement:
(∃ μ : (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M (ev y v 0)) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ,
  (∀ (q : ℚ) (c : J p M (ev y v 0)), μ (q ⊗ₜ[R p] c) = (q : ℂ) * (c : ℂ)) ∧

P.explanation: All original data are universally quantified: p:ℕ, arbitrary field K with CharP K p, integer l with 0≤l<p, arbitrary complex V and Chevalley action, chosen highest vector v, and arbitrary admissible M. H003 expresses the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂ representation by its three action operators, finite dimension l+1, relations and highest vector; these determine the same action via the sl₂ presentation. H005's finite integer basis also being a complex basis is admissibility, and stability under all divided-power generators is equivalent in both directions to U_Z-stability. Conversely the source conclusion gives this nontriviality and every such subspace dichotomy under the same unique lifts. No algebraic-closure assumption, distinct reduced weights, p>2 or l>0 is imposed, so p=2 and l=0 remain included.

import Mathlib
noncomputable section
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LatticeSL2
def scalarRing (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(scalarRing p)
instance (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (scalarRing p).subtype).toAlgebra
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] : Module (R p) V :=
  Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
def divided {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def ev {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev Ix (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
def Stable {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (a : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, a u ∈ W
def SimpleTriple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Stable W x → Stable W y → Stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Preserves {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, a (m : V) ∈ M
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def LiftOf {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (a : Module.End ℂ V) (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, (f m : V) = a (m : V)
def E {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) ℂ V) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
instance (p : ℕ) (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] :
    IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
def L {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V)
def J {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (e : V) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (L p M).comap ((LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ).smulRight e |>.restrictScalars (R p))
def pPart {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) (MR p M) :=
  Submodule.span (R p) (Set.range (fun u : MR p M => (p : ℤ) • u))
abbrev Red {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := ZMod p ⊗[ℤ] MR p M
abbrev RK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  K ⊗[R p] MR p M
abbrev FK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharP K p] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  K ⊗[ZMod p] Red p M
def throughR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (RK κ M) :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K
def throughF {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharP K p]
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (f : Module.End ℤ M) : Module.End K (FK p K M) :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  (((f.baseChange (R p)).restrictScalars ℤ).baseChange (ZMod p)).baseChange K
def matrixUnit {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    {l : ℤ} (B : Module.Basis (Ix l) F U) (i j : Ix l) : Module.End F U :=
  (B.coord j).smulRight (B i)
def genFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End F U) (b : Ix l → U) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ix l, x (b i) = if hi : 0 < i.val then
      ((l - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • b ⟨i.val - 1, Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le i.val 1) i.isLt⟩
      else 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Ix l, y (b i) = if hi : i.val + 1 < l.toNat + 1 then
      ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • b ⟨i.val + 1, hi⟩ else 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Ix l, h (b i) = ((l - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def iotaSpec {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r : R p) (m : M), f (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = (algebraMap (R p) ℂ r) • (m : V)
def canonicalR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (C : RK κ M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M) : Prop :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  ∀ (c : K) (r : R p) (m : M),
    C (c ⊗ₜ[R p] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (κ r * c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m
def pureR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] (κ : R p →+* K)
    {M : Submodule ℤ V} (c : K) (u : MR p M) : RK κ M :=
  letI := κ.toAlgebra
  c ⊗ₜ[R p] u
def canonicalF {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharP K p]
    (κ : R p →+* K) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (D : FK p K M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M) : Prop :=
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∀ (c : K) (a : ZMod p) (r : R p) (m : M),
    D (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (a ⊗ₜ[ℤ] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m))) =
      ((ZMod.cast a : K) * κ r * c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m
def basisOrigin {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] {l : ℤ}
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V)
    (β : Module.Basis (Ix l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ J p M (ev y v 0) ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧
  ∃ ι : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V, iotaSpec p M ι ∧ Function.Injective ι ∧
  ∃ B : Module.Basis (Ix l) (R p) (MR p M),
    (∀ i, ι (B i) = b • ev y v i.val) ∧
  ∃ κ : R p →+* K, ∃ C : RK κ M ≃ₗ[K] VK K M,
    canonicalR κ M C ∧ ∀ i, β i = C (pureR κ 1 (B i))
end LatticeSL2
open LatticeSL2

artifact.representation: λ is the integer l; nonnegative exponents are Nat and I is Fin (l.toNat+1), identified with 0≤i≤λ using H002. V is an arbitrary complex module; x,y,h are its linear action endomorphisms. H003 records the sl₂ Chevalley relations, highest weight and complex irreducibility. M is an arbitrary Submodule ℤ V, equivalently an additive subgroup, with the integer/complex basis and divided-power stability in H005. R is the rational subring generated by inverses of integers not divisible by p; T006 proves it is exactly the specified ℤ_(p). Scalar actions use its inclusion R→ℚ→ℂ. MR is the actual R⊗ℤ M; its image L is used only through the checked iota in T006/T008. J is the coefficient submodule defined by membership in L. VK=K⊗ℤ M uses the tensor commutor identification with the source M⊗ℤ K. Operators are the actual scalar extensions of compatible integral endomorphisms; existence is proved, and compatible lifts are unique. Red=ZMod p⊗ℤ MR is identified with MR/pMR by T018, and FK is its extension to K. RK and FK install only canonical scalar actions internally. matrixUnit B i j sends B j to B i and other basis vectors to zero; multiplication of endomorphisms is composition with the right factor acting first. No Audit A note is a premise, verified Lean theorem or instance assumption; the two M declarations are used directly from pinned Mathlib.
